question: For each positive integer $n$, let $S(n)$ denote the sum of the digits of $n$.  For how many values of $n$ is $n+S(n)+S(S(n))=2007$?
solution:
Both digit sums are positive, so n ≤ 2006. For n ≤ 1999, the digit sum is at most 1+9+9+9 = 28; for 2000 ≤ n ≤ 2006, it is at most 8. Thus S(n) ≤ 28, and S(S(n)) ≤ 10 (the largest digit sum up to 28 is 10). Hence n ≥ 2007−28−10 = 1969.

Since 10 ≡ 1 modulo 9, every integer is congruent to its digit sum modulo 9. The equation therefore gives 3n ≡ 2007 ≡ 0 modulo 9, so n is a multiple of 3. Checking those multiples in the required range gives:

n | S(n) | S(S(n)) | total
1971 | 18 | 9 | 1998
1974 | 21 | 3 | 1998
1977 | 24 | 6 | 2007
1980 | 18 | 9 | 2007
1983 | 21 | 3 | 2007
1986 | 24 | 6 | 2016
1989 | 27 | 9 | 2025
1992 | 21 | 3 | 2016
1995 | 24 | 6 | 2025
1998 | 27 | 9 | 2034
2001 | 3 | 3 | 2007
2004 | 6 | 6 | 2016

The total is 2007 for 1977, 1980, 1983, and 2001.
Final answer: 4
